verification.note: addons/intelligence/tests/test_z_pickup_evaluate.py:165-172 now builds `expected` with the eight fresh_h{7,30,90,365}_f{0,0.5} rows and asserts `[name.rstrip("*") for name in rows] == expected`. Those row names are new in this feature: evaluate.py:350 builds them, evaluate.py:372 adds the `*` mark, and evaluate.py:448 ranks them. That means the old six-name `list(rows)` assertion must have been edited in this change. Spec §7 (docs/specs/pickup-recency.md:232-242) and the touch points (lines 298-300) list only five existing tests: accuracy_worker, worker, retrieval, feed and evaluate_after. test_z_pickup_evaluate.py is not among them, and nothing under docs/process/reviews/feature-pickup-recency mentions it. The edit does not loosen the test: it still asserts the exact row order, and stripping the `*` is needed because the shipped-constants row is now marked. So this is a documentation gap in the touch-point list, not a weakened check. Without git I could not see the diff directly; I inferred the edit from the new row names.

specification_compliance: Spec §7 says existing tests are updated only where they pin version 3, and lists five. The update to test_z_pickup_evaluate.py is a sixth file, outside that list. It is needed because replay now emits the fresh_* rows and the `*` mark.
regression_risks: The `rstrip("*")` normalisation means this test does not check which row carries the `*` mark. That is presumably covered by test_z_pickup_evaluate_after.py, which I did not verify.
